atlas-qa.0093: Treating a Qatar University or Education City fair as open to all: Education City’s is for Qatar Foundation students and alumni, and the Doha Institute’s is aimed at its own students and graduates.
atlas-qa.0094: EY’s Doha graduate programme for nationals asks for excellent written and verbal communication in Arabic and English; we found no posting for foreign graduates that states a level.
atlas-qa.0095: Standard employment contracts are registered in Arabic and English, and the Qatar Living CV guide asks you to state your Arabic level and says Arabic matters more for government, semi-government and some customer-facing roles. No source tested English at work; this is our reading.
atlas-qa.0096: Law 12 of 2024 gives Qataris priority in private jobs, and Qatar Living says Arabic matters more for government and semi-government roles; the national programmes read are for Qataris and run in Arabic and English.
atlas-qa.0097: IT postings for foreigners are mostly for experienced staff, and we found no page testing English or Arabic for graduates in software, data or cybersecurity. This is our reading.
atlas-qa.0098: The World Bank’s modelled youth unemployment rate for Qatar was 0.559% in 2025 (0.573% in 2024); it is a modelled series and says nothing about graduates specifically, and we found no return-offer or time-to-first-job figure for Qatar.
atlas-qa.0099: Foreign nationals were 94% of Qatar’s total workforce and 83% of its private workforce in 2023, so the market for a foreign graduate is large, but roles inside the nationalisation scheme are reserved for Qataris.
atlas-qa.0101: Qatar University, HBKU or an Education City campus sponsors the visa, converted on arrival into a student residence permit after the medical and fingerprints. You need proof of funds or a full scholarship.
atlas-qa.0102: Qatar is not in the Apostille Convention: previous degrees need the full consular legalisation chain. Students may work only on campus, up to 20 hours a week, or in internships registered on Sahem.
atlas-qa.0103: visa QAR 200 + medical QAR 100 + QID QAR 500
atlas-qa.0104: There is no internship visa. Internships through Sahem are only for students already resident in Qatar; an internship on a visa waiver is illegal work, and companies almost never sponsor a temporary work visa for one.
atlas-qa.0106: Graduates of a Qatari university aged 18 to 28 can extend residence one year to look for work, and move to an employer without leaving. Others get a 30-day grace period.
atlas-qa.0108: The employer obtains a quota and registers your contract with the labour ministry, then issues the work entry visa; in Doha you complete the medical, fingerprints and Qatar ID within 30 days. The employer must pay every visa and recruitment cost.
atlas-qa.0109: Since 2020 you may change employer without a no-objection certificate, giving one or two months’ notice. The QFC and free zones process skilled hires faster.
atlas-qa.0111: visa QAR 300 + medical QAR 100 + QID QAR 1,000 a year
atlas-qa.0112: Short unpaid visits need a visit visa sponsored by the university or Qatar Foundation; longer or paid ones a research residence permit. Labs are closed to tourists.
atlas-qa.0113: PhD students funded by the QRDI Council’s GSRA receive a tax-free stipend with housing and tuition covered.
atlas-qa.0116: Qatar has no working-holiday agreements; unauthorised work means up to three years in prison, a QAR 50,000 fine and a Gulf-wide ban.
atlas-qa.0117: EU citizens get a free waiver on arrival, valid 180 days, for up to 90 days in Qatar, not extendable; health insurance is compulsory.
atlas-qa.0119: British citizens get a free 30-day waiver, extendable once for 30 days through Metrash.
atlas-qa.0122: Qatar is not in the apostille convention: Italian and EU documents and degrees go through a five-step consular legalisation chain, ending at the Foreign Ministry in Doha.
atlas-qa.0123: The 90-day visa waiver is for tourism only: for work, study or an internship your employer or institution sponsors you, starting with a work entry visa issued through Metrash (QAR 300, paid by the company).
atlas-qa.0124: Register your National Address on Metrash within 60 days. Residential leases are registered with the Municipality, which you need for family sponsorship.
atlas-qa.0125: After the infectious-disease screening at the Medical Commission, the Qatar ID (QID) is printed, valid 1 year (QAR 1,000, paid by the company), and sent by Q-Post. Do not leave Qatar before it is printed: the entry visa lapses and the process starts again from abroad.
atlas-qa.0126: A positive result for HIV, hepatitis B or C, or lung scars from tuberculosis, even healed, means the permit is refused and you are deported.
atlas-qa.0127: The QID number is your identifier for government services through Metrash.
atlas-qa.0128: Health insurance is compulsory for all non-Qataris; for residents, your employer pays it in full.
atlas-qa.0129: Open an account with your employer’s salary certificate; it is linked to the Wages Protection System. Landlords usually ask for 12 post-dated cheques: a bounced cheque is a crime that brings a travel ban, and the bank freezes the account when the final settlement arrives at the end of a job.
atlas-qa.0130: Neither the entry stamp nor the application receipt lets you work: working before the work visa is issued is a crime punished with arrest, fines up to QAR 50,000 and deportation.
atlas-qa.0131: Leave Qatar before the Qatar ID is printed and the entry visa lapses: the process restarts from abroad.
atlas-qa.0132: A positive test for HIV, hepatitis B or C, or TB scarring, even healed, means unfitness and deportation.
atlas-qa.0133: Landlords want 12 post-dated cheques; banks freeze your account at the final settlement, and a bounced cheque is a crime with a travel ban.
atlas-qa.0134: Some employers answer a resignation with a false “absconding” report that freezes your ID.
atlas-qa.0135: Overstaying a visit costs QAR 200 a day from the first day.
atlas-qa.0136: Converting a tourist visa to a work visa inside Qatar is listed at QAR 500 but granted at the ministry’s discretion.
atlas-qa.0137: Family visas formally need QAR 10,000 a month (6,000 with company housing); salaries in between are decided case by case.
atlas-qa.0138: Sector quotas for hiring Qataris are set by changing ministerial decrees.
